title: Advanced Linux Administration
subtitle: Jeopardy Review

jeopardyFormatExample.clueText: This command displays the first 10 lines of a file

categoryLegend: Files & Archives: head, cp -r, mkdir, touch, tar.  Permissions & ACLs: chown, sticky bit, minimum ACL, setfacl, getfacl.  Networking & DNS: ip link, ping -w, MX records, /etc/resolv.conf, Ctrl-C.  System & Shell: /etc/fstab, swap, uptime, let, shell comments.  Boot, Services & Legacy: Boot from Hard Disk, chkconfig, rcapache2, Traffic-vis, rsync.

clues.clue: This command displays the first 10 lines of a file by default, making it the quickest way to preview a log or config.
This cp flag causes the copy operation to descend into subdirectories, preserving the entire directory tree at the destination.
This command creates a new, empty directory at the path you supply. Supply -p to also build any missing parent directories.
Running this command on an existing filename updates its access and modification timestamps to the current time; running it on a new filename creates an empty file.
This archive container format bundles multiple files and directories into a single file without compression by default; the .gz or .bz2 extension is added when a compressor is piped in.
This command changes both the owning user and the owning group of a file in a single call, using the syntax user:group as its argument.
Set on a shared directory such as /tmp, this special permission bit prevents users from deleting or renaming files that belong to other users.
Every file has this baseline ACL that mirrors the three standard Unix permission entries: owner, owning group, and other.
clues.response: What is the minimum ACL (owner, owning-group, other)?

clues.clue: This command modifies a file's access control list, letting you grant or revoke permissions for named users or groups beyond the traditional owner/group/other model.
This command reads and displays a file's full ACL in a human-readable format, showing every named user, named group, and mask entry.
This ip command variant brings a network interface named eth0 to an operational state, equivalent to the older ifconfig eth0 up.
clues.response: What is ip link set eth0 up?

clues.clue: This ping flag sets a hard deadline in seconds; once the deadline expires the command exits regardless of how many packets have been sent.
This DNS record type designates the mail server responsible for accepting email on behalf of a domain.
clues.response: What is an MX (Mail Exchanger) record?

clues.clue: The Linux resolver reads this file to determine which DNS servers to query and what search domain to append to unqualified hostnames.
While ping is running in a terminal, pressing this key combination sends SIGINT to the process, stopping it and printing the packet-loss summary.
This system file contains the list of filesystems to mount at boot, including the swap partition and any additional block devices.
This partition type acts as overflow RAM: the kernel pages out inactive memory segments to it so physical RAM can serve active processes.
This command prints how long the system has been running and displays three load-average figures representing the past 1, 5, and 15 minutes.
This Bash built-in command performs integer arithmetic directly in a shell script, for example: let result=count+1.
In a shell script, every line that begins with this single character is treated as a comment and is ignored by the interpreter at runtime.
On a SUSE installer boot menu, selecting this option bypasses the installation workflow and loads the operating system already present on the hard disk.
clues.response: What is "Boot from Hard Disk"? (SUSE installer boot-menu option)

clues.clue: This legacy SysV command removes the apache2 web-server service from the init runlevels so it no longer starts automatically at boot. (Modern equivalent: systemctl disable apache2)
clues.response: What is chkconfig apache2 off? (modern: systemctl disable apache2)

clues.clue: On SUSE systems using SysV init, this rc-style wrapper script was the standard way to stop the apache2 service from the command line. (Modern equivalent: systemctl stop apache2)
clues.response: What is rcapache2 stop? (modern: systemctl stop apache2)

clues.clue: This older network-analysis program visualizes active connections from the local host to remote hosts, showing which processes hold those connections. (Modern equivalent: iftop or ss)
clues.response: What is Traffic-vis? (modern: iftop or ss -tn)

clues.clue: This utility efficiently copies complete directory trees across a network to another computer, transferring only changed blocks and preserving permissions, making it the standard tool for remote backups.
